scope: CBSE Class 6 Social Science · Exploring Society: India and Beyond · Chapter 1 · Locating Places on the Earth
claimBoundary: This is deterministic readiness validation using synthetic learner scenarios. It is not a live student study, school pilot, efficacy trial, attainment claim, accessibility certification, or school-specific pacing validation.
passRule: Every scenario must map to an implemented Chapter 1 topic, a Kiki misconception/remediation path, at least one linked required assessment type, a privacy-safe learner action, and an observable mastery criterion.

scenarios.need: Learner reads a map as a picture and estimates real distance from visual length without applying the stated scale.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: visual route length treated as real-world distance
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a fictional map, identify the scale, measure a marked route, convert the map distance to real distance, and explain why appearance alone is insufficient.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Independently converts distances correctly on two unfamiliar fictional maps and justifies each result using the stated scale.

scenarios.need: Learner identifies a symbol or destination correctly but ignores direction or the map legend when describing where one place lies relative to another.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Read a fictional legend and north arrow, then describe two routes using the destination symbol, cardinal direction and distance together.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Uses scale, direction and legend together to interpret two new map relationships without relying on unlabeled visual guesses.

scenarios.need: Learner swaps latitude and longitude or confuses the direction in which the reference lines run with what each coordinate measures.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use an imaginary globe grid to label the Equator and Prime Meridian, then classify latitude as north/south position and longitude as east/west position before locating points.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Correctly interprets four unfamiliar coordinate pairs and explains which value gives north-south position and which gives east-west position.

scenarios.need: Learner omits N/S/E/W or assumes one coordinate alone identifies a precise global position.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: incomplete coordinate treated as precise location
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Complete fictional coordinate cards by adding hemisphere labels and both coordinate values, then compare points that share one coordinate but differ in the other.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Builds and compares three complete coordinate pairs with correct hemisphere notation and no request for the learner's real-world location.

scenarios.need: Learner links local-time difference to latitude or reverses the east/west relationship between longitude and local solar time.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: time difference attributed to latitude or east-west direction reversed
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Compare fictional longitude pairs, calculate angular difference, convert using 15 degrees as approximately one hour, and state which location has later local solar time.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Solves three unfamiliar longitude-time comparisons and consistently identifies the eastward location as later in local solar time.

scenarios.need: Learner assumes official time zones are perfect 15-degree strips or that every country must use exactly one standard time zone.
scenarios.expectedMisconception: official time-zone rules treated as pure longitude geometry
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Separate a geographic local-time calculation from an official-clock statement and explain why legal or administrative time-zone boundaries can depart from ideal longitude strips.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Distinguishes local solar-time reasoning from official standard-time rules in two new examples and avoids universal one-zone claims.

scenarios.need: Learner needs an offline or low-bandwidth path and cannot depend on video, GPS, microphone, camera, cloud AI or personal-data collection to complete the chapter task.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use cached text, a printed or locally drawn fictional map and locally available assessment prompts; complete the reasoning in writing or by local selection without sharing personal location data.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes a map-reading task and mastery check using local resources only, with no network-dependent tutoring or precise-location disclosure.

scenarios.need: Learner understands individual ideas but loses accuracy when scale, coordinates and time reasoning are presented as one long multi-step instruction.
scenarios.safeLearnerAction: Use a Kiki step sequence: identify the geographic question, choose the relevant reference system, calculate one quantity at a time, then state a bounded conclusion.
scenarios.masteryCriterion: Completes one scaffolded and one independent multi-step location/time task while selecting only the map or coordinate information relevant to each step.
